name: commons-coins-v1
description: ⭐ THE COMMONS WITH COINS (Dean, 10/09/2026), THE ARM, and it is built as an ARM and not as the default on purpose: measure it against the shipped commons on identical reference-v15 seeds, put the numbers in front of Dean, and only then flip anything. The design is docs/commons-coins-handoff-2026-09-10-v2.md, rules K1-K15. THE RULE IN ONE LINE: the bonus is EITHER play a card OF THE BOARD'S COLOUR onto it and take that board's plain action (two cards of any colours standing in as one, both landing on the pile), OR discard every card on one central pile and take ONE COIN PER CARD; coins have exactly two uses, the Farmstead's suit power and the Endgame cards, and Harvest never reaches the centre at all. ⛔ EVERY PASSENGER IS PINNED BY NAME AND HERE IS THE LIST, because the 05/09/2026 lesson is that ruling an arm in rules in its whole bundle and the meeple supply cap shipped at 2 that way without anybody arguing for it. SEVEN KNOBS, and nothing else in the game moves: (1) rules.turn.visitCurrency 'commons' - the shipped default, pinned so the arm cannot silently stop being the commons if the default ever flips again; (2) rules.turn.bonusTiming 'start' - the shipped order, K2, bonus first because a turn visibly ends on the main action; pinned for the same reason; (3) rules.turn.commonsTake 'coins' - THE MINT, K3/K4: the slot's second option becomes discard every card on one central pile to their suits' discard piles and take ONE COIN PER CARD, no card paid, not offered on an empty pile (K5), and Harvest never reaches the centre at all (K4, reversing C5), so commonsHarvestMin and commonsHarvestTake have no subject and the farm bypass reads 0% by construction; (4) rules.economy.commonsColourMatch true - THE GATE, K3: the card you play must match the board's suit; it is the one lever measured to land the bonus rate inside Dean's band on its own (34.4% of turns against a shipped 58.9%); (5) rules.economy.commonsWildPair true - THE PAIR, D5/D7 of the commons pass, BUILT FOR THE FIRST TIME: two cards of any colours pay for one board of any colour and both land on the pile, which is what the 09/09/2026 colour-match arm did NOT have, so that arm's 34.4% is the gate at its harshest and this arm should read somewhere between it and 58.9%; (6) rules.economy.endgameCoinCost 3 - SINK ONE, K15: the fifteen Endgame cards cost 3 coins and no cards, while the fifteen Power cards keep their two-own-suit cost, so each currency has one kind of card; (7) rules.economy.farmsteadCoinPower true - SINK TWO, K10-K14: the Farmstead becomes a building with no threshold whose activation cost is one coin, used as a GROW that is your MAIN action, once per turn, nothing placed on it, with a unique per-suit power (rules.economy.farmsteadPower.*, four numbers, Wheat's power carrying none) and its own end-game scorer MOVED TO THE BARN rather than deleted (K13). No rent: a rival may never use your Farmstead (K14). ⭐ WHY THIS SHAPE AND NOT ANOTHER, in one paragraph, because four variants were measured on 09/09/2026 and every one of them fell short in the same place. The shipped commons puts the bonus at the top of Dean's band (58.9% of turns) but feeds barns from the middle: 63% of harvested barn cards came out of central piles, so the farm engine was demoted to decoration. Every rule ON the piles failed to move that share, because the centre is a closed system and every card played into it reaches somebody's barn. Every rule that sent pile cards BACK TO HANDS - the free take, take-and-spend, the paid take - fixed the barn and ran the bonus at 74% to 89% of turns, because the cards taken paid for more plays. This arm keeps the colour gate, makes the piles worth clearing WITHOUT turning them back into cards, and gives the coins two uses that are both dearer than the supply. ⛔ COINS WERE DELETED ON 02/09/2026 (v31) AND EVERY EARLIER COIN ECONOMY IN THIS PROJECT DIED OF A SECOND FAUCET OR A PITY RATE, so read the arithmetic before the numbers: EXACTLY ONE MINT (clearing a pile, K8) and EXACTLY TWO SINKS (the Farmstead and the Endgame cards, K7). Coins score nothing, break no ties, buy no ordinary card and are minted by nothing but a pile; leftover coins are dead. island.tileRule.coinsPerDelivery stays pinned at 0 and is a tombstone, not a faucet. If a future session finds itself adding a third use or a second mint, that is the old failure repeating rather than a tuning. ⭐ WHAT TO READ, IN ORDER (§4 of the handoff). (1) The bonus rate ON THE TURN MEASURE, by seat count, against 30-60%, split PLAY / COIN TAKE / SLOT UNSPENT - prediction: play about 35-45% with the pair, take about 10%, total mid-band. ⚠️ Judging the band on plays per turn rather than turns cost this project a re-run on 09/09/2026 and A Helping Hand is worth about ten points of the difference. (2) Coins minted per player per game (prediction 7-9), spent on the Farmstead against on Endgame cards, and HELD AT GAME END - if dead coins exceed about two a player the sinks are too dear. (3) FARMSTEAD FIRES BY SUIT, which is the imbalance reading Dean raised by name: if one suit fires twice as often as another the POWERS are mispriced, not the coins. (4) Farm bypass, 0% by construction, then the barn glut (it should PASS, as it has under every variant with no centre-to-barn flow) and deliveries per player. (5) The door mix - Apiary took 36% to 49% of plays in every commons arm so far and the colour gate should spread it. (6) Own-crop build share: ⛔ ONLY ONE MONOCULTURE PULL LEAVES, not both, because K13 moves the own-crop scorer to the Barn rather than deleting it, so expect a SMALL move off 82.6-83.3% and read a large one as the coin economy rather than the price. (7) Winning scores and their sources, Endgame cards now coin-gated. (8) Game length, action inflation, suite time and branching - the wild pair adds C(h,2) fee options per board, which is 21 a board and 105 a turn at the engine's hand bound of 7. ⚠️ HOW TO RUN IT: --overlay= with --watchlist, never --sweep=, and always --n=1580 (4,820 games, five mirrors, reference-v15 seeds). A bare --watchlist is a 1,580-game pilot and must not be quoted beside a real run. Stay on reference-v15: the arm is PAIRED on its seeds against reports/watchlist-2026-09-09T16-41-51-reference-v15.txt (the shipped commons) and ...T17-03-32-...-commons-colour-match-v1.txt (the measured gate). Cut reference-v16 only when Dean rules the arm in. ⚠️ AND THE ENGINE'S HAND LIMIT OF 7 IS THE SIMULATOR'S BOUND AND NOT A RULE OF THE GAME (C7): the table plays with none, and every report header must say so. Its two paired sub-arms are overlays/commons-coins-no-wild-v1.overlay.json (what the wild pair is worth) and overlays/commons-coins-endgame-cards-v1.overlay.json (what pricing the Endgame cards in coins is worth), and overlays/commons-coins-endgame-price.sweep.json prices that card at 2, 3 and 4. UNBUILT AND UNRUN BEFORE THIS PASS. ⛔ PASSENGERS PINNED 12/09/2026: Dean's plain-action balloon and Village Store ruling moved sixteen shipped leaves at once. This overlay predates that flip and every report taken against it does too, so each of those leaves is pinned here BY NAME at its PRE-FLIP value. Without it an arm read as a delta against a pre-flip base would silently gain a one-card flight, an always-present Aerodrome and a live coin economy. That is the 05/09/2026 passenger lesson: an overlay that should not move with the shipped default has to pin every knob the flip moved.
